Apple earlier this year launched the all-new MacBook Neo, and based on various indications, this laptop has achieved tremendous success. Here's what we currently know about the follow-up to Apple's most affordable laptop…

MacBook Neo 2 Features

A19 Pro Chip

The current MacBook Neo uses the A18 Pro chip, which is the same chip used in the iPhone 16 Pro. According to Bloomberg, Apple is developing a new-generation MacBook Neo equipped with the A19 Pro chip.

In terms of performance, the A19 Pro is approximately 10 to 15% faster than the A18 Pro in single-core and multi-core CPU tests. The improvement in GPU performance is even more significant, with benchmarks showing the A19 Pro's GPU performance increasing by as much as 40%. This is because each GPU core in the A19 Pro has a built-in neural accelerator.

The A19 Pro chip is also used in the flagship iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone Air.

According to journalist Tim Culpan, Apple is likely to use a "binned" version of the A19 Pro chip in the MacBook Neo. Although the A19 Pro chip in the iPhone 17 Pro features a 6-core GPU, the version used in the MacBook Neo will likely only come with a 5-core GPU.

More Memory

One of the trade-offs of the MacBook Neo is that it only has 8GB of RAM. Other Mac product lines under Apple currently start at 16GB of RAM.

The new-generation MacBook Neo will not jump directly to 16GB of RAM, but is expected to come with 12GB of RAM due to the adoption of the aforementioned A19 Pro.

As I mentioned in my review, I don't think the 8GB of RAM in the MacBook Neo is a major limitation. However, an improvement in the new-generation model is still a welcome change.

Brand New AI Features

The upgraded combination of the A19 Pro chip paired with 12GB of RAM is expected to support the more powerful on-device AI models Apple announced at WWDC. This model can provide a more accurate voice dictation experience, as well as new options for customising Siri voices.

The current MacBook Neo does not support this feature because it has the A18 Pro chip and only 8GB of RAM.

New Colours

The MacBook Neo comes in a variety of colourful finishes, including Citrus Yellow, Cherry Blossom Pink, Indigo and Silver. Bloomberg reports that Apple plans to "periodically" update the colours for the MacBook Neo.

As for which colours will be available for the new-generation MacBook Neo, there are no details at this time.

MacBook Neo 2: Release Date and Conclusion

Apple launched the current MacBook Neo this March. Tim Culpan reports that the version equipped with the A19 Pro is expected to launch within 2027.

What changes would you like Apple to make on the second-generation MacBook Neo? Are you a MacBook Neo user? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
